defeaters: Engine-name identity is not session dependence: two fresh isolated sessions may intentionally use the same authorized CLI surface and exact model.
Engine-name diversity is not independence proof: different engine strings cannot prove separate sessions, frozen worklists, frozen submissions, or no cross-access.

Declared reviewer.model is carrier metadata, not proof of requested model, actual model, model ID, CLI version, or returned model metadata. Only the real CLI stream plus its hash-bound canonical external worker record may supply that authority.
Carrier-axis distinction is necessary but incomplete: distinct vote_id, reviewer_id, and lane cannot substitute for the external invocation-record gates required by owner two-vote work.

Semantic laundering remains forbidden: matching gloss text, prose, surface, or engine metadata cannot substitute for canonical schema validity and agreement on the governed conclusion plus reason key.
Schema stuffing is forbidden: fields absent from the canonical artifact must not be invented, copied into ungoverned extension keys, or falsely described as validator-verified.
One session reused for both submissions, a submission exposed across lanes, or a worklist modified after hashing fails the external owner gate even if the generic carrier validates.
A documentation-only claim of independence does not repair the validator, add the focused red-first test, or register it in the complete harness.
definition_of_done: A red-first pure test reproduces the current false rejection of a same-engine pair whose vote_id, reviewer_id, and lane are pairwise distinct.
The generic validator no longer treats equal reviewer.engine values as evidence of dependence.
The validator requires distinct vote_id, reviewer_id, and lane values and retains every canonical schema, occurrence, conclusion, reason-key, agreement, and no-gloss semantic gate.
The validator's CLI and self-test success wording truthfully describes carrier-level validation only and does not claim external session or model-identity proof.
The three narrowly scoped authority documents consistently distinguish canonical carrier validation from the mandatory external worker-record gate for owner two-vote work.

A closed qamus.two_vote_worker_record.v1 schema and validator require reviewer_id and lane, private cli_executable_path, redacted_argv, fallback_model_configured false, requested_model, actual_model, model_id, cli_version, session_id, start_sha, branch, worktree, permitted_files, frozen worklist-envelope and submission hashes, real CLI model-proof artifact plus hash, explicit access_to_other_reviewers_work false, and no_cross_access true. A closed oneOf requires either output_artifact_path plus output_artifact_sha256 or commit_sha plus commit_tree_sha256.

Pair validation requires distinct reviewer, lane, session, output, and frozen-submission identities; each reviewer remains unable to read the other submission until both are frozen and hashed. A real Opus 5 or Sonnet 5 identity is established only by the external CLI invocation and returned metadata named by the worker record, never by schema validity or a synthetic self-test fixture.

When a consuming owner packet requires Opus 5 or Sonnet 5, its lane policy must require requested_model, actual_model, and model_id to equal claude-opus-5 or claude-sonnet-5 exactly, forbid fallback, and reject silent substitution. This generic packet defines the proof carrier but does not choose reviewers or models.

No existing canonical carrier schema or artifact is changed. The additive qamus.two_vote_worker_record.v1 schema governs private external proof separately; no external-proof field is inserted into either two-vote carrier schema.
No fact is certified, reclassified, promoted, revoked, or written, and no owner, scholar, certifier, public, website, or deployment authority is created.

TP-PVN-REANCHOR-HARNESS-INTEGRATION-W1 exclusively owns later shared harness and golden-command updates; this packet's focused suites, validator self-tests, canonical sample validation, complete unchanged harness, exact frozen-start changed-path allowlist, protected-artifact drift check, and git diff --check all pass.

guards: The method transfers and linguistic conclusions never do: this deterministic packet changes only carrier-validator independence accounting, the separate external worker-record schema and validator, focused tests, and directly contradictory authority wording.
Equal reviewer.engine values are allowed when vote_id, reviewer_id, and lane are distinct and all canonical schema and semantic checks pass.
Distinct vote_id, reviewer_id, and lane are mandatory carrier-level axes. Empty, malformed, duplicated, or schema-invalid values fail closed.
Canonical conclusion and reason agreement remains recomputed from both complete votes. Gloss text, free prose, declared flags, engine, model, and lane never establish semantic agreement.

Generic tools/validate_two_vote_artifacts.py validation proves only the artifact fields and semantics it can inspect. Its output must not claim independent CLI sessions, verified actual model identity, frozen inputs, or no cross-access.

For owner two-vote work, external worker records are a separate mandatory gate. Each closed record requires reviewer_id, lane, cli_executable_path, redacted_argv, fallback_model_configured false, requested_model, actual_model, model_id, cli_version, session_id, start_sha, branch, worktree, permitted_files, worklist_envelope_sha256, frozen_submission_sha256, model_proof_artifact_path, model_proof_sha256, access_to_other_reviewers_work false, and no_cross_access true. Its closed output oneOf requires either output_artifact_path plus output_artifact_sha256 or commit_sha plus commit_tree_sha256.

The pair validator recomputes every referenced hash, requires distinct reviewer, lane, session, output, and frozen-submission identities, and refuses comparison until both worklists and submissions are frozen. It does not inspect credentials and it does not let either reviewer access the other's work.

The real non-interactive Claude CLI invocation and returned metadata are the only model-identity authority. cli_executable_path and machine topology remain private under out. A qamus.two_vote_worker_record.v1 row binds that external proof but cannot create it, and a schema-valid or synthetic record never proves Opus 5 or Sonnet 5.

A consuming packet that requests claude-opus-5 or claude-sonnet-5 must match that exact string in requested_model, actual_model, and model_id, must record a no-fallback invocation, and must reject any substituted or unproven model.
The existing reviewer.model field remains governed carrier metadata but is not silently reinterpreted as returned actual-model proof.
No field absent from qamus/schemas/two-vote-artifact.schema.json is added to an artifact. A proposed schema change is outside this packet and routes to owner review.
No artifact, fact, certification event, reason registry, public payload, website file, or live surface is writable.

Start only from a clean isolated worktree. Freeze HEAD before edits under out/two-vote-engine-independence-w1/start-sha.txt, enforce the exact tracked plus untracked seven-path changed set from that SHA, run protected canonical-artifact drift separately, and run git diff --check separately.
